name: ARTISAN-SNM
aliases: Axonics SacRal NeuromodulaTIon System for Urinary Urgency Incontinence TreatmeNt
question: Does single-stage implantation of the rechargeable Axonics sacral neuromodulation system, without an external test phase, reduce urgency urinary incontinence episodes in adults?

arms.label: Rechargeable Axonics sacral neuromodulation system implanted in one nonstaged procedure

design.population: Adults aged 21 or older with urgency urinary incontinence for at least 6 months (at least four leaks on a 72-hour diary, at least half associated with urgency), excluding stress or mixed incontinence, mechanical obstruction and bladder pain syndrome; 129 implanted (age 59.3 years, range 21 to 86; 98% women).
design.description: Prospective, multicenter, single-arm, unblinded pivotal study
design.locator: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03327948 (eligibility); PMC7384085 Results, Study participants (age, sex); FDA SSED pp25, 33 (153 enrolled, 129 implanted; 15 US and 5 Western European sites)

verdictNote: Single-arm study; 90% of implanted patients were responders at 6 months, with no comparator.
takeaway: In 129 adults with urgency urinary incontinence, single-stage implantation of the rechargeable Axonics sacral neuromodulation system without a test phase gave 90% responders at 6 months (episodes 5.6 to 1.3 per day) and no serious device-related adverse events; there was no comparator.

reports.label: 6-month results
reports.citation: McCrery R, Lane F, Benson K, et al. "Treatment of Urinary Urgency Incontinence Using a Rechargeable SNM System: 6-Month Results of the ARTISAN-SNM Study." *J Urol.* 2020;203(1):185-192. doi:10.1097/JU.0000000000000458

results.measure: 6-month responder rate (at least 50% fewer urgency incontinence episodes on a 3-day diary), all implanted patients, as-treated
results.note: Prespecified test was a responder rate above 50% (one-sided binomial). Per the FDA review of the same analysis: 116/129 (89.9%; 95% CI 83.4% to 94.5%), P<0.0001.

results.measure: Mean episodes per day, baseline to 6 months (mean ± SE)
ICIQ-OABqol improvement at 6 months (0 to 100 scale)
results.note: Described as clinically meaningful; FDA review: HRQL score 51.5 to 85.6, with 10 points the minimal important difference.

harms.label: Device-related and procedure-related adverse events through the 2019-01-18 data lock

values.single: 13/129 (10.1%) with device-related events; 13/129 (10.1%) with procedure-related events (15 events)

harms.note: No device- or procedure-related serious events. Procedural pain was the most common procedure-related event (4 patients); implant-site pain, extremity pain and vulvovaginal pain or discomfort each occurred in 2 patients.

delivery.label: Implant technique
delivery.value: Tined lead and rechargeable neurostimulator implanted in one nonstaged procedure, without an external test phase.

delivery.label: Enrollment and sites
delivery.value: 153 patients enrolled and 129 implanted: 97 at 15 US sites and 32 at 5 Western European sites.

reports.label: 1-year results
reports.citation: Benson K, McCrery R, Taylor C, et al. "One-year outcomes of the ARTISAN-SNM study with the Axonics System for the treatment of urinary urgency incontinence." *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2020;39(5):1482-1488. doi:10.1002/nau.24376
reports.followUp: 1 year after implant; 124 of 129 completed the visit

results.measure: 1-year responder rate (at least 50% fewer urgency incontinence episodes), all implanted patients, as-treated with missing data counted as failures
results.note: Described by the authors as the primary efficacy outcome; no hypothesis test reported at 1 year. Among the 113 patients who were responders at 1 month, 106 (94%) were responders at 1 year.
results.locator: PMC7384085 Results, Therapy responder rate and UUI symptom reduction

results.measure: Mean episodes per day, baseline to 1 year (mean ± SE), all implanted patients
results.note: A 75% reduction. Among 115 responders, 88 (77%) had a reduction of at least 75% and 29% were dry.
results.locator: PMC7384085 Results, Therapy responder rate and UUI symptom reduction; Figure 3

results.measure: ICIQ-OABqol HRQL improvement at 1 year (0 to 100 scale)
results.note: All four subscales improved by more than the 10-point minimal important difference.
results.locator: PMC7384085 Results, Quality of life and therapy satisfaction; Figure 4

results.measure: Satisfied with therapy; would undergo therapy again, all implanted patients
results.note: Missing patients counted as negative responses.
results.locator: PMC7384085 Results, Quality of life and therapy satisfaction; Figure 5A

results.measure: Able to recharge; found recharging easy; found frequency and duration acceptable, among 124 patients available
results.note: Of the 124, 107 (86%) recharged for less than 1 hour per session and 95% went at least 7 days between sessions.

harms.label: Device-related adverse events
harms.note: Ten of the events occurred before 6 months. Stimulation discomfort occurred in 7 patients (5.4%), all resolved with reprogramming; charging-area discomfort or heating in 1, resolved by retraining; neurostimulator-site pain in 2, both resolved spontaneously.

values.single: 2 patients (1 lead migration; 1 high impedance with suspected lead fracture)

harms.label: Surgical interventions
harms.note: Two were explants in initial nonresponders for continued lack of efficacy.

harms.label: Exits before 1 year
harms.note: System explant in 4 (1 infection, 1 pain unrelated to the device, 2 insufficient efficacy) and 1 death unrelated to the device or procedure. No unanticipated or serious device-related or procedure-related adverse events.

delivery.label: Lead placement and testing
delivery.value: Fluoroscopically guided tined lead along S3 (preferred) or S4; a response on at least two electrodes at less than 4 mA was required for full implant, and no patient failed this.

delivery.label: Recharging instruction
delivery.value: Patients were told to recharge every 1 to 2 weeks with a wireless charger held over the neurostimulator by a belt.

reports.label: Satisfaction analysis
reports.citation: Geynisman-Tan J, Mueller MG, Kenton KS. "Satisfaction with a rechargeable sacral neuromodulation system-A secondary analysis of the ARTISAN-SNM study." *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2021;40(1):549-554. doi:10.1002/nau.24596

results.measure: Very, moderately and slightly satisfied at 1 year (7-point Likert scale), among 124 patients with complete data
results.note: Satisfaction was associated with diary efficacy: very satisfied patients had larger reductions in voids, leaks, urgent leaks and desperate-urgency voids per day.

results.measure: Patients who were nonresponders at 1 month and were responders at 1 year
results.note: Twelve of the 14 month-1 nonresponders continued to improve between 1 month and 1 year.

reports.label: 2-year results
reports.citation: Pezzella A, McCrery R, Lane F, et al. "Two-year outcomes of the ARTISAN-SNM study for the treatment of urinary urgency incontinence using the Axonics rechargeable sacral neuromodulation system." *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2021;40(2):714-721. doi:10.1002/nau.24615
reports.followUp: 2 years after implant; 121 of 129 completed the visit
reports.followUpLocator: PMC7986436 Results, Study demographics and baseline symptoms

results.measure: 2-year responder rate (at least 50% fewer urgency incontinence episodes), completers analysis (the report's primary analysis)
results.note: The responder count of 113 is taken from Figure 3B. As-treated across all 129 implanted patients: 88% (113/129). Among test responders (responders at 1 month): 97% (106/109 available).
results.locator: PMC7986436 Results, Therapy responder rate and UUI symptom reduction; Figure 2

results.measure: Mean episodes per day, baseline to 2 years (mean ± SE), completers
results.note: An 82% reduction. Of the 113 responders, 93 (82%) had a reduction of at least 75%, 54% had a reduction above 90% and 37% were dry; these percentages use responders as the denominator.
results.locator: PMC7986436 Results, Therapy responder rate and UUI symptom reduction; Figure 3

results.measure: ICIQ-OABqol HRQL improvement at 2 years (0 to 100 scale), completers
results.locator: PMC7986436 Results, Quality of life; Figure 4

results.measure: Satisfied with therapy; would undergo therapy again, among 121 completers
Able to recharge; rated recharging easy; rated it acceptable; sessions under 1 hour; at least 7 days between sessions, among 121 completers

harms.label: Device-related and procedure-related adverse events through 2 years
harms.note: No unanticipated or serious device-related or procedure-related adverse events. Uncomfortable stimulation was the most common device-related event (11 patients, 9%): resolved by amplitude adjustment in 2 and reprogramming in 9. Neurostimulator-site pain occurred in 2 patients.

harms.label: Surgical interventions
harms.note: Lead revision in 3 (migration 1, high impedance 2; efficacy returned in all); neurostimulator revision in 4 (infection 1, pain 1, migration or rotation 2, attributed to abdominoplasty); explant without reimplant in 5 (infection 1, pain unrelated to the device 1, insufficient efficacy 3).

harms.label: Exits before 2 years
harms.note: System explant in 5, lost to follow-up in 1, insufficient efficacy with device hibernation in 1, and 1 death unrelated to the device or procedure.

harms.label: MRI studies
harms.note: Eight of the body, spine or torso; five of the head or neck. No adverse events or lead migrations followed any MRI.

delivery.label: Neurostimulator placement and charging
delivery.value: Neurostimulator placed near the upper buttock; participants were told to recharge every 1 to 2 weeks.

delivery.label: Prior external trial
delivery.value: Nine patients had passed an external trial stimulation before enrollment without a full implant; all nine were responders at every visit, and excluding them left the responder rates unchanged (88% as-treated; 93% completers).

relations.note: The authors compared responder-rate analysis, neurostimulator-site pain and lead migration with InSite's non-rechargeable InterStim experience.
